explanation: A title that shows respect and reverence for God, acknowledging his sovereignty and authority.
A people descended from Jacob (also called Israel), who was the son of Isaac and grandson of Abraham. They are God's chosen people in the Old Testament.
An ancient kingdom in Northeast Africa where the Israelites were held as slaves under Pharaoh's rule.
The supreme leader and ruler of Egypt, regarded as a divine figure in Egyptian mythology.
A Jewish festival that commemorates the deliverance of the Israelites from slavery in Egypt under Moses' leadership.
A lamb that was sacrificed and eaten during the Passover feast as a symbol of God's protection and deliverance.
A spiritual being sent by God to strike down the firstborn in Egypt as part of the ten plagues.
The blood of the Passover lamb, which was to be smeared on the doorframes of Israelite homes to protect them from the angel of death.
The term used to describe the Israelites' escape from Egypt and their journey toward the promised land, Canaan.
The final and most severe of the ten plagues that God sent upon Egypt to compel Pharaoh to release the Israelites.
